主要内容: The document titled '40-F' is a filing by Brookfield Asset Management Inc. with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). It is an annual report pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013. The report includes the Annual Information Form, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Results (MD&A), and Consolidated Financial Statements for the same period. The filing also incorporates certifications and disclosures regarding controls and procedures. The company is incorporated in Ontario, Canada, and its principal executive offices are located in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The report indicates that the company has filed all required reports during the preceding 12 months and has been subject to such filing requirements for the past 90 days. The document outlines the registrant's disclosure controls and procedures as of December 31, 2013, indicating that these controls were effective at the reasonable assurance level. The registrant's principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that the controls ensured timely reporting and communication of required information. It is noted that while these controls provide reasonable assurance, they cannot prevent all errors and fraud. The registrant's management also assessed the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, concluding that it was effective as of December 31, 2013, with no material weaknesses identified. The document outlines the financial reporting and compliance practices of Brookfield Asset Management Inc. for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013. It includes the Attestation Report of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, which is incorporated by reference into the Annual Report on Form 40-F. The report confirms that there were no changes in internal control over financial reporting that materially affected the registrant's operations. The registrant has also adopted a Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, which applies to its principal officers and is available on its website. The document further details the composition of the audit committee and the independence of its members, as well as information on principal accountant fees and pre-approval policies. The document outlines the corporate governance practices of Brookfield Asset Management Inc., a U.S.-based financial services company. It highlights the composition of the board of directors, emphasizing that 11 out of 16 directors are independent as defined by NYSE rules. The company maintains an independent audit committee with members such as George S. Taylor, Marcel R. Coutu, and Diana L. Taylor. The document also details the communication channels for shareholders to interact with independent directors, including contact via email or mail. Additionally, it mentions the company's adherence to NYSE corporate governance guidelines, which are posted on its website. The information is part of the company's annual report on Form 40-F, filed with the SEC on March 31, 2014.
